newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE dealers complain of fewer terminals.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE dealers complain of fewer terminals.

text.p: Dealers on South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange said they were finding trade difficult after the exchange asked them to restrict the number of terminals used following earlier system problems.
"We are only doing half the work. We are connected in on half the terminals. We can't operate like this," a dealer said.
Another dealer said volumes were limited due to the fewer number of terminals allowed to be used for trading.

The JSE said it had asked brokers to restrict the number of terminals in use as a precautionary measure after it reverted back to the old JET 1 system following three days of problematic trade with the JET 2 system installed last weekend.
"This is done as a precaution. We will be increasing the number of terminals in use in the afternoon," JSE president Roy Andersen told Reuters.

The JSE said earlier on Thursday that it would revert back to the old JET 1 system until problems with JET 2 had been ironed out. JET 2 was taken down last night and will be returned to suppliers for re-evaluation, the JSE said.

System problems this week resulted in trade being halted twice on Monday and the opening of the bourse delayed by an hour on Tuesday. On Wednesday only 27 minutes of trade took place as technicians battled with new JET system.
